Above is my indie game Merri Puzzle on Steam. It is a physics based puzzle game. I saw a lot of people doing roll a ball through a maze, or get to the end of a maze type games. I really loved and enjoyed them as a kid (you would always get these from wendy's or dairy queen. So I decided to make one myself. I had not gone any game dev in YEARS before this, so it was a bit scary. I learned a lot quickly. The best advice I can give to people is take bad criticism, and work from it. You shouldn't have a hissy fit in the comment sections on green light or where ever you are trying to post your game to get it published. Negative comments are better than positive ones as it identifies flaws in your game. My games graphics were not to many peoples liking, so I re-did them 5 times! Eventually I got the votes to get green lit. I have had lack luster sales and success, but the journey was wonderful! I did a huge content update recently as well to address some of the feedback and e-mails I have gotten. This was my first attempt at getting something on steam as well, there is a lot I would do differently now as well!

I think the hardest thing for your game is promotion. Indie DB and other sites that do give always help a good amount.

If I am wanting to publish a game on steam in the next year, how would I do it?

Okay, so first and for most, you need your game concept idea. Next find out what engine you want to build it with. If game dev takes you over one year, do not get discouraged, just keep at it. Make sure to let people in on the process and give you advice. Generally speaking, negative feedback over what to change and where to improve is better than positive feedback. In addition, when you do have your game finished and bug tested, you will need to apply to steamworks. This is their back end for developers to use to publish their games. I signed a NDA so I cannot say a lot about it, but I would advise you pick a game engine like unity for 3-d or game maker for 2, since both of these have direct support for steams SDK, and make it super easy to get things packaged and setup. You also want to think about art assets you will need before launch. Examples would be if you want to do trading cards, or achievements. There are templates out there for both.

As far as getting hype for your game for release, do a kick starter for exposure. Make the rewards decent, and make sure that you post in as many places as you can. Tell everyone, tell your friends, tell your friends friends, ask people to help spread the word. There are places like players me that have smaller youtubers who will play your game as well. The most exposure you can get, the better. Feel free to send beta test versions as well, steam has a way to do this easily for you. You can do that to help get beta testers to show your product before it launches, but still have control over it. Marketing and branding is something you want to think about before you consider publishing. I know it sounds simple, but I found marketing to be even harder than making the game.

As for after launch, or beta launch, take negative criticism and use it. Learn from mistakes to build a better product. If you get comments that just say this game sucks, do not bother responding to them or engaging as that kind of user will simply just be hostile with nothing real to gain.

If you get a comment like your game is shit because ____, then think about that reasoning and see if you can make improvements to the issue. Ultimately your games success depends on how people enjoy it.

If I didn't answer anything, please let me know.
